To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the photosynthetic system of leaves in natural canopy has a large capacity to adjust to the light environment and the adjustment is targeted to balance the partial processes of photosynthetic electron and energy transport, but the adjustment does not lead to a high efficiency use of nitrogen in the photosynthetic machine.

(1) the photosynthetic control mechanisms are able to adjust the rate of photosynthesis to meet the plant requirements and to balance the capacity of partial reactions of photosynthetic electron and carbon transport, (2) the photosynthesising apparatus is down-regulated in shade-adjusted plants, and (3) nitrogen is not used at its full efficiency in the photosynthetic components of shade plants.

the rate parameters of photosynthetic reactions adjust to the natural growth irradiance, but the adjustment is not complete, and the photosynthetic capacity is still in excess of the photosynthesizing capacity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the adjustment of the photosynthesizing apparatus to the light conditions in which a leaf develops.
the regulation of the photosyn-thesis rate and its components in leaves that grow under different light environments, and with the nitrogen partitioning in these leaves.
the regulation of the photosynthesizing apparatus, the adjustment of the light reactions to the dark reactions and the role of the photosyntheis control systems in this process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the adjustment of the photosynthesizing machinery to shade is not a simple linear process.

the adjustment of the photosynthesizing leaf to shade is a result of the adjustment of the light-harveting machinery, the electron transport chain, and the Calvin-Benson cycle, and the adjustment of the regulation of these components.

, in the natural canopy, the adjustment of photosynthesis to shade is not a matter of a single rate parameter but a complex phenomenon that is achieved through the down-regulation of several rate parameters of the photosyntheses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the photosynthetic capacity is adjusted to the growth light, but the adjustment is not perfect, because it is not possible to adjust all rate parameters simultaneously.
photosynthesis is down-regulated in the shade to match the actual rate of photosynthesis to a lower light level and to avoid overproduction of energy, which would lead to photooxidative damage.
the adjustment of leaf photosynthesis in shade is a result of down-regulation of the partial processes of photosynthetic carbon fixation and electron transport.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the photosynthetic system is a very flexible system that can adjust to a wide range of growth light.
shade leaves do not have a lower capacity of photosynthesis, but they do not use it to full extent, and this is a consequence of a strong down-regulation of the photosyntheses machinery.
the adjustment of photosynthesis in natural canopies is a complex process that involves a number of rate parameters of the photosyntheses apparatus.
